more_info.overview: Lanolin is the waxy material recovered from sheep wool. It contains a complex mixture of long-chain esters, together with smaller amounts of related alcohols, acids and hydrocarbons. Its protective role on wool and its wax-like consistency distinguish it from a simple triglyceride oil. FDA lists lanolin as a plasticising material in chewing-gum base. That specified gum-base use is a different technological role from the historical glazing classification.
more_info.origin: Animal-derived material recovered from sheep wool during wool washing and separation, then refined. It is a complex wool-wax preparation rather than a single purified molecule.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: Lanolin is an animal-derived wool wax and is not vegan. The reviewed identity source does not establish vegetarian suitability or halal and kosher certification of a food-use preparation.
more_info.uses: Used as a plasticising or softening material in chewing-gum base under 21 CFR 172.615.
more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use follows the preparation-specific conditions in 21 CFR 172.615, checked in 2026.
